- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

owner: product-authority

updated: 2026-08-23
---

# Base writing style

These rules apply to everything written for a human reader, regardless of
document type. Document types add a format layer on top of this base; they
never override it.

## Goal

The reader gets the point of any paragraph in one read, any section in 30
seconds, and the whole document in two minutes. Write for the first read.

## Lead with the point

At every scale, state the conclusion first and the support after.

- A document opens with what it found or decided, not how it got there.
- A section opens with its main claim, then evidence.
- A paragraph opens with its point, then elaboration.

If a document type defines a structure, that structure is just this rule
applied to that type. If no structure is defined, use this rule to invent
one.

## Detail placement

Precision serves the point; it never precedes it. Formal specification
language, methods, raw data, scoring tables, and citations go after the
claim they support — or in an appendix. The body is for understanding.

## Sentences

- One idea per sentence.
- Active voice, with a named actor: "Reviewers delete unlinked checks,"
  not "Unlinked checks are subject to deletion."
- Prefer the short common word: "use" not "utilize," "end" not
  "terminate," "before" not "prior to."

## Terminology

- Never use a metaphor as a technical term. If a word describes a thing
  by what it resembles instead of what it literally does, replace it with
  the literal description. Test: could a competent reader from outside
  the team work out the meaning from the words alone? If not, rewrite.
- Banned words. Never use these, in any form:
  - "load-bearing" → say "other work depends on it" or "critical to
    operations"
  - "surface" (as in context surface, config surface) → say "input,"
    "source," or "channel"
  - "seam" → say "boundary" or "integration point"
  - "scar tissue" → describe the actual problem, e.g. "an unreviewed
    workaround that was never removed"
- Explain every insider reference — a past incident, an internal system,
  a person — in one plain sentence, or cut it. Assume the reader knows
  none of our history.

## Style examples

These examples exist only to show sentence style. The domain (a public
library) is deliberately unrelated to our work. Copy the style; never
copy the content or vocabulary into real documents.

bad:

> Unreturned inventory constitutes scar tissue on the circulation loop
> and rapidly becomes load-bearing for downstream shelving throughput.

good:

> Overdue books pile up at the front desk, and staff spend their time
> reshelving late returns instead of helping visitors.

The bad sentence uses two metaphors as terms and never names an actor.
The good sentence says who is affected and what actually happens, in
plain words.

| 1 | 2026-08-14 | update | Authored (seed layer); earlier history, if any, in the repository history. |
| 1 | 2026-08-19 | state | draft → approved. |

   121	  BC-shop is a component team in the product literature's sense: it
   122	  receives bounded work for its context and does not own a feature end
   123	  to end; a request that crosses contexts is decomposed above it, in
   124	  the initiative, never by the shops between themselves.
   125	- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
   126	  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
   127	  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
   128	  same shape whoever performs it.
   129	- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
   130	  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
   131	  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
   132	  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
   133	  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
   134	- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
   135	  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
   136	  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
   137	  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
   138	  kernel, or separate ways.
   139	- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
   140	  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
   141	  wording.
   142	- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
   143	  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
   144	  internals.
   145	- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
   146	  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, the
   147	  outcome it serves, and the contract it entered through; the
   148	  exclusive decision of `lead-pm`; written as the first section of an
   149	  initiative and nowhere else.
   150	- **initiative** — the product-level problem artifact: one problem
   151	  worth solving, stated for the product, with its framing, one
   152	  measured outcome, an appetite and no-gos, the feasibility and
   153	  usability attachments, and the solutions architect's decomposition;
   154	  made by the PM role, screened by the cold reviewer, bet on by the
   155	  authority; features are made from it.
   156	- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario in a feature that
   157	  states, as a requirement, what counts as done for one behavior;
   158	  co-produced by the PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop;
   159	  assigned to that context by a `@bounded-context:<name>` tag the
   160	  solutions architect writes; held in that shop's scenario register.
   161	- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
   162	  acceptance scenarios tagged to it across all features, with their
   163	  hashes and states; read in full across every context when a claim
   164	  spans contexts.
   165	- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
   166	  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
   167	  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
   168	  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
   169	- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
   170	  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
   171	  domain the question falls in.
   172	- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
   173	  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
   174	  contract between contexts.
   175	- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
   176	  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
   177	  PO role.
   178	- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
   179	  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
   180	  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
   181	  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
   182	  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
   183	  together as the `assistant` guideline.
   184	- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
   185	  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
   186	  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
   187	  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
   188	  role's exclusive domain.
   189	- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
   190	  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
   191	- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
   192	  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
   193	  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
   194	- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
   195	  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
   196	  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
   197	  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
   198	- **feature** — a Gherkin Feature: one capability from the user's or
   199	  agent's point of view — a narrative saying who, what, and the outcome
   200	  — with the acceptance scenarios that state what counts as done for
   201	  it; product-level, belonging to its framing or initiative; its
   202	  scenarios may be owned by several Bounded Contexts. The PO role's
   203	  artifact. (The per-shop *brief* was retired 2026-08-28; the
   204	  `decision-brief` to the authority is unrelated.)
   205	- **check of record** — the check whose verdict the definitions rely
   206	  on for an artifact when the role that makes it also holds the
   207	  authority that approves it; for the initiative, the cold reviewer's
   208	  screen.
   209	- **bet** — the authority's decision to spend an initiative's appetite:
   210	  the go/no-go, taken in a review, moving it from `proposed` to
   211	  `planned`.
   212	- **product decision record** — the PO role's record of one
   213	  product-level decision — decision, alternatives, consequences,
   214	  decider and right, reversibility; ADR and MADR forms; checked as PO
   215	  output.
   216	- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
   217	  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
   218	  provenance through every translation and delegation.
   219

     3	description: The product-management role of the lead shop. Frames intent, holds the product's outcome, judges value and viability, orders the roadmap, and checks the PO's output against the framing.
     4	tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob

    14	---
    15	
    16	# Lead PM
    17	
    18	You hold the role where intent enters the shop and where the product's
    19	outcome is answered for. You turn what an originator — whoever expresses intent at the
    20	product's edge — asks for into a recorded *framing* — the problem the shop takes the request to be
    21	about and the outcome it serves — and you check what the PO role makes
    22	from that framing against it. The product authority holds this role in
    23	person; that is the role's authority. Agents assist the role's
    24	activities (see Interfaces); the frontmatter contracts those agents,
    25	and the person holding the role is bound by the definitions, not by
    26	the tool list.
    27	
    28	**Standard of judgment:** outcomes, not outputs — you frame a problem
    29	to solve, never a feature to build. You engage an originator's
    30	statements as an interlocutor and record convergence rather than
    31	inferring it. Material reaches you decidable — a screen verdict, a decision brief,
    32	or an ask (a question a definition cannot answer, sent with a
    33	proposed default) — or it goes back to the role that sent it with the
    34	missing criterion named.
    35	
    36	**Accountable for:**
    37	- The initiative for each problem worth solving, opening with the
    38	  framing of its intent: the originator, the expressed outcome, the
    39	  problem taken to be worth solving, and the contract — product or
    40	  operational — it entered through; the rest of the initiative — one
    41	  measured outcome, appetite and no-gos — drafted by the assisting
    42	  agent and decided here; screened by the cold reviewer as the check
    43	  of record.
    44	- The value and viability judgment on every candidate problem: whether
    45	  it is worth solving and whether the product can sustain the solution.
    46	- The check on the product-owner (PO) role's output — features,
    47	  decision records, backlog order — against the framing, under criteria the definitions state: a
    48	  pass, a fail with the criterion named, or a definition change where
    49	  the criteria proved insufficient.
    50	- Roadmap priority: which framed problems come first, recorded with
    51	  reasons.
    52	- Convergence of each discovery conversation recorded on its anchor
    53	  (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)).
    54	- The provenance chain: any activity traceable to its originating
    55	  expression without ambiguity, and every decision applied to the
    56	  governed artifacts it changes with a Document History entry.
    57	
    58	**Domain (exclusive):** the framing of intent — what the shop takes an
    59	expression to be asking for is decided by this role alone.
    60	
    61	**Decision rights.**
    62	- *Decides:* the framing (exclusive); and, as the accountable role,
    63	  value and viability, roadmap priority, and whether the PO's output
    64	  passes its check — each recorded with its reasons and open to another
    65	  role's evidence.
    66	- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PO with reasons; the outcome a
    67	  shape must serve to the solutions architect.
    68	- *Resolves:* a conflict between this role's framing and another
    69	  role's domain, recorded on the affected artifacts; no role overrides this
    70	  one's framing.
    71	- *Never decides:* feasibility and the stack (the
    72	  [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s);
    73	  authorship of acceptance scenarios and backlog order within the
    74	  framing (the PO's); usability (the
    75	  [product designer](lead-product-designer.md)'s); how a
    76	  Bounded Context builds a behavior (the BC-shop's).
    77	
    78	**Admissible evidence:** the originator's own words, recorded;
    79	discovery-conversation anchors; measured outcomes of shipped work; a
    80	screen verdict — a cold reviewer's judgment against a named criteria
    81	set (a fitness set, a guideline, or the framing itself). Not authoritative: a stakeholder's feature list read as a
    82	requirement; the PO's backlog read as the product's intent; the
    83	role's own reading of every artifact in place of a stated criterion.
    84	
    85	**Interfaces:**
    86	- Originators: intent in; the recorded framing back.
    87	- The PO role: framed intent and its outcome out; features, decision
    88	  records, backlog order, and scope questions in for the check.
    89	- The solutions architect role: framed problem and outcome out;
    90	  feasibility verdict, technical risks, and questions in.
    91	- The product designer role: framed problems and outcomes out;
    92	  usability evidence, prototypes, and observed user needs in.
    93	- Assisting agents: each assisted activity's process names what the
    94	  agent prepares and what this role decides.
    95	- Asks from any role: answered here, and a recurring ask becomes a
    96	  definition change.
    97	
    98	**Knowledge and skills:** product discovery and interviewing; the
    99	four product risks — value, usability, feasibility, viability — and
   100	which role answers for each (value and viability here; feasibility
   101	with the solutions architect; usability with the product designer); the shop's
   102	definition corpus (every activity run through the basis); the
   103	[stakeholder-presentation](../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md)
   104	and [discovery-conversation](../processes/discovery-conversation.md)
   105	processes; the [working principle set](../principles.md) every
   106	activity runs under.
   107	
   108	**Anti-rationalization:**
   109	- "I'll just read the scenarios myself." → A check without a stated
   110	  criterion is a read, not a check; the criterion is the missing
   111	  definition.
   112	- "The PO knows what I meant." → A framing is recorded or it does not
   113	  exist.
   114	- "This feature is obviously worth it." → Value is a judgment with
   115	  evidence named; the feature list is not the evidence.
   116	- "It's infeasible, so the framing is wrong." → Infeasible returns the
   117	  problem for re-framing; it does not decide what is worth solving.
   118	- "I'll decide the how while I'm here." → The how belongs to the
   119	  architect and the shops; deciding it here removes their check.
   120

    16	# Lead Solutions Architect

    18	You hold the role that owns the product's shape: its technical vision — its
    19	technology stack, its Bounded Contexts, their contracts, and who owns
    20	what — is readable from the artifacts you maintain, structural
    21	questions from any shop resolve against them, and the value of what

13	    12	# Glossary
14	    13	
15	    14	## How the list combines
16	    15	
17	    16	The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
18	    17	name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
19	    18	terms uses one of these when one fits.
20	    19	
21	    20	## Terms
22	    21	
23	    22	- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
24	    23	  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
25	    24	- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
26	    25	  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
27	    26	- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
28	    27	  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
29	    28	- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
30	    29	  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
31	    30	- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
32	    31	  enums, required sections.
33	    32	- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
34	    33	  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
35	    34	- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
36	    35	  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
37	    36	- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
38	    37	  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
39	    38	- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
40	    39	  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
41	    40	  into every rendering.
42	    41	- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
43	    42	  scoring an artifact type's quality.
44	    43	- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
45	    44	  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
46	    45	- **role** — a named capability contract and set of accountabilities,
47	    46	  assigned by process steps to whoever fills it; sequencing lives in
48	    47	  process definitions, not roles.
49	    48	- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
50	    49	  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
51	    50	  definition).
52	    51	- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
53	    52	  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
54	    53	- **owner** — the role that approves changes to a definition; named in
55	    54	  every definition's frontmatter.
56	    55	- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
57	    56	  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
58	    57	- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
59	    58	  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
60	    59	- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
61	    60	  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
62	    61	- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
63	    62	  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
64	    63	  archive.
65	    64	- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
66	    65	  context it loads into: working (every activity), architecture (the
67	    66	  designed system), or experience (the product's interactions).
68	    67	- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
69	    68	  artifact, never loaded into context.
70	    69	- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
71	    70	  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
72	    71	- **anchor** — the governed record a conversation attaches to: a session
73	    72	  record, a review record, or a work item; carries the conversation's
74	    73	  state across transcript boundaries.
75	    74	- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
76	    75	  (anchor: a review record and its outcomes), or work (anchor: a work
77	    76	  item).
78	    77	- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
79	    78	  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
80	    79	- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority decides
81	    80	  on presented material. Replaces "sitting".
82	    81	- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
83	    82	  presented and the outcomes applied; each decision traces in the
84	    83	  changed artifacts' Document History, never in a standing ledger.
85	    84	- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
86	    85	  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
87	    86	- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
88	    87	  failsafe exit fires.
89	    88	- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, keep,
90	    89	  retire, or terminal, with its target.
91	    90	- **authority-call** — a row marker on a migration-plan row awaiting a
92	    91	  decision from the authority; not an action — the row has no effect and
93	    92	  is out of scope for any run until ruled.
94	    93	- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
95	    94	  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
96	    95	- **close-out** — the mechanical execution of the migration plan's
97	    96	  pre-decided retire and terminal actions: snapshot, delete, archive
98	    97	  move, a loud post-check, and the branch promotion; no review loop.
99	    98	  All stages run consecutively at cut-over.
100	    99	- **snapshot tag** — the annotated git tag (`pre-migration`) on `main`'s
101	   100	  pre-execution commit, preserving the full corpus for terminal-recovery;
102	   101	  after close-out a terminal record exists only there.
103	   102	- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
104	   103	  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
105	   104	- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
106	   105	  running, held, done, cancelled.
107	   106	- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
108	   107	  anchor, by inactivity or by an ask; a held run is resumed or
109	   108	  cancelled, never dropped.
110	   109	- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
111	   110	  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
112	   111	- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
113	   112	  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).
114	   113	- **Bounded Context** — a deliberately drawn region of the product with
115	   114	  one internal language, one model, and one set of contracts to other
116	   115	  regions; drawn by design, never discovered after the fact (Evans,
117	   116	  *Domain-Driven Design*).
118	   117	- **shop** — the entity that builds, operates, and evolves part of the
119	   118	  product. Two types: the lead shop (the system-level coordinator; owns
120	   119	  product-level artifacts and no Bounded Context) and the BC-shop (owns
121	   120	  and produces exactly one Bounded Context). By the owner's decision a
122	   121	  BC-shop is a component team in the product literature's sense: it
123	   122	  receives bounded work for its context and does not own a feature end
124	   123	  to end; a request that crosses contexts is decomposed above it, in
125	   124	  the initiative, never by the shops between themselves.
126	   125	- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
127	   126	  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
128	   127	  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
129	   128	  same shape whoever performs it.
130	   129	- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
131	   130	  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
132	   131	  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
133	   132	  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
134	   133	  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
135	   134	- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
136	   135	  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
137	   136	  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
138	   137	  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
139	   138	  kernel, or separate ways.
140	   139	- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
141	   140	  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
142	   141	  wording.
143	   142	- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
144	   143	  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
145	   144	  internals.
146	   145	- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
147	   146	  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, the
148	   147	  outcome it serves, and the contract it entered through; the
149	   148	  exclusive decision of `lead-pm`; written as the first section of an
150	   149	  initiative and nowhere else.
151	   150	- **initiative** — the product-level problem artifact: one problem
152	   151	  worth solving, stated for the product, with its framing, one
153	   152	  measured outcome, an appetite and no-gos, the feasibility and
154	   153	  usability attachments, and the solutions architect's decomposition;
155	   154	  made by the PM role, screened by the cold reviewer, bet on by the
156	   155	  authority; features are made from it.
157	   156	- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario in a feature that
158	   157	  states, as a requirement, what counts as done for one behavior;
159	   158	  co-produced by the PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop;
160	   159	  assigned to that context by a `@bounded-context:<name>` tag the
161	   160	  solutions architect writes; held in that shop's scenario register.
162	   161	- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
163	   162	  acceptance scenarios tagged to it across all features, with their
164	   163	  hashes and states; read in full across every context when a claim
165	   164	  spans contexts.
166	   165	- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
167	   166	  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
168	   167	  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
169	   168	  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
170	   169	- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
171	   170	  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
172	   171	  domain the question falls in.
173	   172	- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
174	   173	  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
175	   174	  contract between contexts.
176	   175	- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
177	   176	  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
178	   177	  PO role.
179	   178	- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
180	   179	  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
181	   180	  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
182	   181	  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
183	   182	  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
184	   183	  together as the `assistant` guideline.
185	   184	- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
186	   185	  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
187	   186	  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
188	   187	  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
189	   188	  role's exclusive domain.
190	   189	- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
191	   190	  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
192	   191	- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
193	   192	  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
194	   193	  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
195	   194	- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
196	   195	  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
197	   196	  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
198	   197	  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
199	   198	- **feature** — a Gherkin Feature: one capability from the user's or
200	   199	  agent's point of view — a narrative saying who, what, and the outcome
201	   200	  — with the acceptance scenarios that state what counts as done for
202	   201	  it; product-level, belonging to its framing or initiative; its
203	   202	  scenarios may be owned by several Bounded Contexts. The PO role's
204	   203	  artifact. (The per-shop *brief* was retired 2026-08-28; the
205	   204	  `decision-brief` to the authority is unrelated.)
206	   205	- **check of record** — the check whose verdict the definitions rely
207	   206	  on for an artifact when the role that makes it also holds the
208	   207	  authority that approves it; for the initiative, the cold reviewer's
209	   208	  screen.
210	   209	- **bet** — the authority's decision to spend an initiative's appetite:
211	   210	  the go/no-go, taken in a review, moving it from `proposed` to
212	   211	  `planned`.
213	   212	- **product decision record** — the PO role's record of one
214	   213	  product-level decision — decision, alternatives, consequences,
215	   214	  decider and right, reversibility; ADR and MADR forms; checked as PO
216	   215	  output.
217	   216	- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
218	   217	  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
219	   218	  provenance through every translation and delegation.

260	    15	
261	    16	# Lead PM
262	    17	
263	    18	You hold the role where intent enters the shop and where the product's
264	    19	outcome is answered for. You turn what an originator — whoever expresses intent at the
265	    20	product's edge — asks for into a recorded *framing* — the problem the shop takes the request to be
266	    21	about and the outcome it serves — and you check what the PO role makes
267	    22	from that framing against it. The product authority holds this role in
268	    23	person; that is the role's authority. Agents assist the role's
269	    24	activities (see Interfaces); the frontmatter contracts those agents,
270	    25	and the person holding the role is bound by the definitions, not by
271	    26	the tool list.
272	    27	
273	    28	**Standard of judgment:** outcomes, not outputs — you frame a problem
274	    29	to solve, never a feature to build. You engage an originator's
275	    30	statements as an interlocutor and record convergence rather than
276	    31	inferring it. Material reaches you decidable — a screen verdict, a decision brief,
277	    32	or an ask (a question a definition cannot answer, sent with a
278	    33	proposed default) — or it goes back to the role that sent it with the
279	    34	missing criterion named.
280	    35	
281	    36	**Accountable for:**
282	    37	- The initiative for each problem worth solving, opening with the
283	    38	  framing of its intent: the originator, the expressed outcome, the
284	    39	  problem taken to be worth solving, and the contract — product or
285	    40	  operational — it entered through; the rest of the initiative — one
286	    41	  measured outcome, appetite and no-gos — drafted by the assisting
287	    42	  agent and decided here; screened by the cold reviewer as the check
288	    43	  of record.
289	    44	- The value and viability judgment on every candidate problem: whether
290	    45	  it is worth solving and whether the product can sustain the solution.
291	    46	- The check on the product-owner (PO) role's output — features,
292	    47	  decision records, backlog order — against the framing, under criteria the definitions state: a
293	    48	  pass, a fail with the criterion named, or a definition change where
294	    49	  the criteria proved insufficient.
295	    50	- Roadmap priority: which framed problems come first, recorded with
296	    51	  reasons.
297	    52	- Convergence of each discovery conversation recorded on its anchor
298	    53	  (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)).
299	    54	- The provenance chain: any activity traceable to its originating
300	    55	  expression without ambiguity, and every decision applied to the
301	    56	  governed artifacts it changes with a Document History entry.
302	    57	
303	    58	**Domain (exclusive):** the framing of intent — what the shop takes an
304	    59	expression to be asking for is decided by this role alone.
305	    60	
306	    61	**Decision rights.**
307	    62	- *Decides:* the framing (exclusive); and, as the accountable role,
308	    63	  value and viability, roadmap priority, and whether the PO's output
309	    64	  passes its check — each recorded with its reasons and open to another
310	    65	  role's evidence.
311	    66	- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PO with reasons; the outcome a
312	    67	  shape must serve to the solutions architect.
313	    68	- *Resolves:* a conflict between this role's framing and another
314	    69	  role's domain, recorded on the affected artifacts; no role overrides this
315	    70	  one's framing.
316	    71	- *Never decides:* feasibility and the stack (the
317	    72	  [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s);
318	    73	  authorship of acceptance scenarios and backlog order within the
319	    74	  framing (the PO's); usability (the
320	    75	  [product designer](lead-product-designer.md)'s); how a
321	    76	  Bounded Context builds a behavior (the BC-shop's).
322	    77	
323	    78	**Admissible evidence:** the originator's own words, recorded;
324	    79	discovery-conversation anchors; measured outcomes of shipped work; a
325	    80	screen verdict — a cold reviewer's judgment against a named criteria
326	    81	set (a fitness set, a guideline, or the framing itself). Not authoritative: a stakeholder's feature list read as a
327	    82	requirement; the PO's backlog read as the product's intent; the
328	    83	role's own reading of every artifact in place of a stated criterion.
329	    84	
330	    85	**Interfaces:**
331	    86	- Originators: intent in; the recorded framing back.
332	    87	- The PO role: framed intent and its outcome out; features, decision
333	    88	  records, backlog order, and scope questions in for the check.
334	    89	- The solutions architect role: framed problem and outcome out;
335	    90	  feasibility verdict, technical risks, and questions in.
336	    91	- The product designer role: framed problems and outcomes out;
337	    92	  usability evidence, prototypes, and observed user needs in.
338	    93	- Assisting agents: each assisted activity's process names what the
339	    94	  agent prepares and what this role decides.
340	    95	- Asks from any role: answered here, and a recurring ask becomes a
341	    96	  definition change.
342	    97	
343	    98	**Knowledge and skills:** product discovery and interviewing; the
344	    99	four product risks — value, usability, feasibility, viability — and
345	   100	which role answers for each (value and viability here; feasibility
346	   101	with the solutions architect; usability with the product designer); the shop's
347	   102	definition corpus (every activity run through the basis); the
348	   103	[stakeholder-presentation](../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md)
349	   104	and [discovery-conversation](../processes/discovery-conversation.md)
350	   105	processes; the [working principle set](../principles.md) every
351	   106	activity runs under.
352	   107	
353	   108	**Anti-rationalization:**
354	   109	- "I'll just read the scenarios myself." → A check without a stated
355	   110	  criterion is a read, not a check; the criterion is the missing
356	   111	  definition.
357	   112	- "The PO knows what I meant." → A framing is recorded or it does not
358	   113	  exist.
359	   114	- "This feature is obviously worth it." → Value is a judgment with
360	   115	  evidence named; the feature list is not the evidence.
361	   116	- "It's infeasible, so the framing is wrong." → Infeasible returns the
362	   117	  problem for re-framing; it does not decide what is worth solving.
363	   118	- "I'll decide the how while I'm here." → The how belongs to the
364	   119	  architect and the shops; deciding it here removes their check.

399	    16	# Lead Solutions Architect
400	    17	
401	    18	You hold the role that owns the product's shape: its technical vision — its
402	    19	technology stack, its Bounded Contexts, their contracts, and who owns
403	    20	what — is readable from the artifacts you maintain, structural
404	    21	questions from any shop resolve against them, and the value of what
405	    22	is delivered against that vision is yours to answer for.
406	    23	
407	    24	**Default posture:** pre-state determines the vehicle. The pre-state
408	    25	— what a Bounded Context actually is before a change — is read from
409	    26	its contracts and never from its internals; it, not the request's
410	    27	wording, decides which message type the request travels in. Decide
411	    28	only what is hard to reverse; bound everything
412	    29	else. No design decision stands unscreened against the architecture
413	    30	principles (the conformance accountability below).
414	    31	
415	    32	**Accountable for:**
416	    33	- The feasibility verdict for every framed problem and every feature —
417	    34	  whether the product can be built as framed with the stack, capacity,
418	    35	  and time it has — with its reasons recorded.
419	    36	- The structural model of the product, maintained as an artifact
420	    37	  readable without the code.
421	    38	- The product-wide technology stack and platform guardrails, each
422	    39	  recorded as an architecture decision record with its reasons and the
423	    40	  bound it sets for Bounded Context shops.
424	    41	- The decomposition: subdomain-to-Bounded-Context assignments and the
425	    42	  relationship kind of each contract between contexts, recorded with
426	    43	  reasons.
427	    44	- The scenario-register loop: every checked feature's scenarios each
428	    45	  tagged `@bounded-context:` with the context that owns it, dispatched
429	    46	  to that shop, and work returned verified against that assignment
430	    47	  through the shops' scenario registers.
431	    48	- Conformance of architecture activities to the
432	    49	  [architecture principle set](../architecture-principles.md): every
433	    50	  structural decision, contract, and architecture decision record
434	    51	  screened against it; a principle a design cannot satisfy is an
435	    52	  exception escalated to the authority and recorded, never a deviation
436	    53	  absorbed.
437	    54	
438	    55	**Domain (exclusive):** the stack — which technologies the product is
439	    56	built on is decided by this role alone.
440	    57	
441	    58	**Decision rights.**
442	    59	- *Decides:* the platform guardrails that bound the stack; the
443	    60	  decomposition — which Bounded Context owns a capability; integration
444	    61	  strategy and each contract's relationship kind; the product's
445	    62	  non-functional requirements.
446	    63	- *Recommends:* enabler work — technical work that makes features
447	    64	  possible — into the PO's backlog.
448	    65	- *Escalates to the authority:* a design that cannot satisfy an
449	    66	  architecture principle — the role never grants itself an exception;
450	    67	  contract-breaking changes; cross-context conflicts; any stack
451	    68	  decision that commits the product
452	    69	  to a vendor or a recurring cost above the threshold the authority
453	    70	  sets when it approves this role — until set, every such commitment
454	    71	  escalates.
455	    72	- *Bounds, never approves:* Bounded Context shops choose within the
456	    73	  guardrails; a choice outside them is raised as a contract question,
457	    74	  not vetoed.
458	    75	
459	    76	**Admissible evidence:** a Bounded Context's contracts; a sweep of
460	    77	every context's scenario register, never one context's copy;
461	    78	architecture decision records in source control; published package
462	    79	data — the upstream registry's own metadata for a package. Not
463	    80	authoritative: a local copy of published data, spike
464	    81	findings, forward-looking prose, and code reachable only by entering
465	    82	a Bounded Context.
466	    83	
467	    84	**Interfaces:** the PM role — framed intent arrives, feasibility and
468	    85	shape return; the PO role — checked features arrive for assignment,
469	    86	enabler recommendations return, the backlog is structured to mirror
470	    87	the decomposition, and the count of initiatives touching more than one
471	    88	context, per quarter, arrives as the signal to review the
472	    89	decomposition; Bounded Context shops — messages of a
473	    90	defined type out, clarify questions and returned work in; the
474	    91	authority — escalations. Clarify questions on structure, stack,
475	    92	contracts, and decomposition are answered by this role.
476	    93	
477	    94	**Knowledge and skills:** the
478	    95	[architecture principle set](../architecture-principles.md) — the
479	    96	standard every design decision is checked against — and the

775	    22	# Process: PO output check
776	    23	
777	    24	**Purpose:** Check a piece of the PO role's output against the PM
778	    25	role's framing under criteria the definitions state, so that the PM
779	    26	role decides from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion
780	    27	named, or a definition change — and never by reading every artifact.
781	    28	
782	    29	**Guiding statement:** The check is the criteria applied, not the
783	    30	checker's reading. A finding the criteria cannot name is a missing
784	    31	criterion, and the decision that follows is a definition change, not a
785	    32	verdict on the maker.
786	    33	
787	    34	**Outcomes:**
788	    35	- O1. The output — a feature, a product decision record, or a backlog
789	    36	  order — is screened against a named criteria set and the framing it
790	    37	  claims to serve — witnessed by `screen`'s inputs and the
791	    38	  `screen-review` it returns.
792	    39	- O2. The PM role decides from the review and round log; the artifact
793	    40	  reaches the PM role only through the findings' quotes — witnessed by
794	    41	  `decide`'s inputs, which exclude the artifact.
795	    42	- O3. Every screen round is recorded and the loop exits on a clean
796	    43	  verdict, on findings no criterion names, or at the round cap —
797	    44	  witnessed by `log-round` and `route-screen`.
798	    45	- O4. A fail names the criterion missed; a definition change names the
799	    46	  gap, and the gap is filed in the named definition's Document History
800	    47	  — witnessed by the `check-decision` fields and `record`'s
801	    48	  `definition` and `gap_entry` outputs.
802	    49	- O5. A question the framing cannot answer leaves the run as an ask to
803	    50	  the PM role, with a default, and the run resumes — witnessed by
804	    51	  `revise`'s `asks` and the `ask` value.
805	    52	
806	    53	**Roles:** maker — [`../roles/lead-po.md`](../roles/lead-po.md)
807	    54	(submits and revises; never decides its own pass). screener —
808	    55	[`../roles/cold-reviewer.md`](../roles/cold-reviewer.md) (fresh
809	    56	context every round; judges against the criteria). the PM role —
810	    57	[`../roles/lead-pm.md`](../roles/lead-pm.md) (accountable for the
811	    58	decision; a human-held role that decides from the verdict; its
812	    59	assisting agent prepares the record and the gap entry).
813	    60	
814	    61	**Carried by:**
815	    62	[`../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md`](../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md)
816	    63	— generated from this definition by
817	    64	[`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never
818	    65	edited by hand.

840	    87	  route_screen -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — decide with findings open| decide
841	    88	  route_screen -->|else| revise
842	    89	  revise --> advance_round
843	    90	  advance_round --> screen
844	    91	  decide --> record
845	    92	  record --> __end
846	    93	```
847	    94	
848	    95	
849	    96	## Data
850	    97	
851	    98	Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema
852	    99	names inline; every structured shape is a `$ref` to a defined type with
853	   100	an explicit source. Conditions are CEL expressions over these names. A
854	   101	*criteria set* is the approved fitness set or guideline for the
855	   102	artifact's type. The framing is always a criterion, named `framing`;
856	   103	until a criteria set exists for a type, `criteria_path` names the
857	   104	framing itself and `framing` is the only named criterion. The artifact
858	   105	status values this process sets — `checked` on pass, `returned` on
859	   106	fail, `pending-definition` on definition change — are this process's
860	   107	until the artifact typedefs define their own.
861	   108	
862	   109	```yaml
863	   110	data:
864	   111	  artifact: {type: string, format: uri-reference}
865	   112	  framing: {type: string, format: uri-reference}
866	   113	  criteria_path: {type: string, format: uri-reference}
867	   114	  review: {$ref: screen-review, from: ../types/screen-review.md}
868	   115	  round: {type: integer, initial: 1}
869	   116	  round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3}
870	   117	  round_log: {type: array, items: {$ref: screen-review}, initial: []}
871	   118	  ask: {$ref: ask, from: ../types/ask.md, initial: null}
872	   119	  decision: {$ref: check-decision, from: ../types/check-decision.md}
873	   120	  gap_entry: {type: string}
874	   121	  definition: {type: string, format: uri-reference}
875	   122	```
876	   123	
877	   124	## Steps
878	   125	
879	   126	```yaml
880	   127	start: screen
881	   128	parameters: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
882	   129	result: decision
883	   130	steps:
884	   131	  - id: screen
885	   132	    name: Screen against the criteria
886	   133	    run-by: {role: cold-reviewer, execution: agent, fresh-context: true}
887	   134	    inputs: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
888	   135	    outputs: [review]
889	   136	    prompt: |
890	   137	      Read the criteria set at criteria_path, the framing at framing,
891	   138	      and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact
892	   139	      against every criterion and against the framing: does each part
893	   140	      of it trace to the framing, and does anything in it serve no
894	   141	      framed outcome? Report every finding with the criterion it fails
895	   142	      by name — "framing" for a part that does not trace to the framing
896	   143	      or serves no framed outcome — the quoted text, the change, and
897	   144	      whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a
898	   145	      wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides
899	   146	      from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding
900	   147	      with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean"
901	   148	      only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top
902	   149	      three changes.
903	   150	    next: log-round
904	   151	    annotations:
905	   152	      fabro: {model: high-reasoning, node: separate-context-per-round}
906	   153	
907	   154	  - id: log-round
908	   155	    name: Record the round
909	   156	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
910	   157	    inputs: [review, round_log]
911	   158	    set:
912	   159	      round_log: round_log + [review]
913	   160	    next: route-screen
914	   161	
915	   162	  - id: route-screen
916	   163	    name: Route on the screen
917	   164	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
918	   165	    inputs: [review, round, round_cap]
919	   166	    branches:
920	   167	      - label: "success exit: clean"
921	   168	        when: review.verdict == "clean"
922	   169	        next: decide
923	   170	      - label: "definition exit: every finding is uncovered — nothing the maker can repair"
924	   171	        when: size(review.findings) > 0 && review.findings.all(f, f.criterion == "uncovered")
925	   172	        next: decide
926	   173	      - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — decide with findings open"
927	   174	        when: round >= round_cap
928	   175	        next: decide
929	   176	      - else: revise
930	   177	
931	   178	  - id: revise
932	   179	    name: Revise the output
933	   180	    run-by: {role: lead-po, execution: agent}
934	   181	    inputs: [artifact, review, framing, ask]
935	   182	    outputs: [artifact]
936	   183	    asks: [lead-pm]
937	   184	    prompt: |
938	   185	      Repair every finding whose criterion is named, "framing"
939	   186	      included; leave findings marked "uncovered" as they are — they
940	   187	      are the PM role's to decide. If a repair needs something the framing does not say —
941	   188	      the originator's intent, whether a thing is in scope, a decision
942	   189	      another role's domain holds — return an ask to lead-pm instead
943	   190	      of guessing: the question, its kind, the default you will apply
944	   191	      if unanswered, and a checkpoint holding the repairs made so far.
945	   192	      On the first pass ask is absent; if it carries an answer or
946	   193	      resolved defaulted, act on it and finish the repairs.
947	   194	    next: advance-round
948	   195	
949	   196	  - id: advance-round
950	   197	    name: Advance the round
951	   198	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
952	   199	    inputs: [round]
953	   200	    set:
954	   201	      round: round + 1
955	   202	    next: screen
956	   203	
957	   204	  - id: decide
958	   205	    name: Decide on the verdict
959	   206	    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: human}
960	   207	    inputs: [review, round_log, framing]
961	   208	    outputs: [decision]
962	   209	    prompt: |
963	   210	      From the final review and the round log, decide. "pass": the
964	   211	      screen is clean, or its only findings are uncovered and you judge
965	   212	      none of them needs a criterion — say so in the reasons. "fail": a
966	   213	      named criterion, "framing" included, is still missed at the round
967	   214	      cap — name it.
968	   215	      "definition-change": an uncovered finding should have been a
969	   216	      criterion, or a criterion the output met produced something that
970	   217	      does not serve the framing — name the definition and what it
971	   218	      lacks. Where both a missed named criterion and an open uncovered finding
972	   219	      stand at the cap, "fail" takes precedence and the reasons carry
973	   220	      the uncovered finding. Decide from the quotes in the review.
974	   221	      Record your reasons.
975	   222	    next: record
976	   223	
977	   224	  - id: record
978	   225	    name: Record the decision
979	   226	    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: agent}
980	   227	    inputs: [decision, artifact, round_log]
981	   228	    outputs: [artifact, gap_entry, definition]
982	   229	    prompt: |
983	   230	      Write into the artifact's Document History one review entry per
984	   231	      round with its verdict, then a state entry carrying the decision
985	   232	      and its reasons. Set the artifact's status: "checked" on pass,
986	   233	      "returned" on fail with the criterion named, "pending-definition"
987	   234	      on definition-change. On "definition-change", write a review
988	   235	      entry stating the gap into the Document History of the definition
989	   236	      the decision names; return that file's path as definition and the
990	   237	      entry's text as gap_entry. Otherwise return both empty. Return
991	   238	      the artifact.
992	   239	    next: end
993	   240	```
994	   241	
995	   242	## Derived checks
996	   243	
997	   244	| Outcome | Check | Kind | Where |
998	   245	|---|---|---|---|
999	   246	| O1 | screen reads only criteria, framing, artifact | judged | `screen.prompt` and inputs |
1000	   247	| O2 | `artifact` absent from `decide.inputs` | mechanical | `decide.inputs` |
1001	   248	| O3 | every round logged; three labeled exits | mechanical | `log-round`, `route-screen` |
1002	   249	| O4 | `criterion` present on fail, `gap` on definition-change; `definition` and `gap_entry` non-empty on definition-change | judged | `check-decision`, `record` outputs |
1003	   250	| O5 | `revise` carries `asks`; process carries `ask-cap`; `ask` listed in inputs | mechanical | `revise`, frontmatter |
1004	   251	
1005	   252	## Document History
1006	   253	
1007	   254	| Version | Date | Kind | Entry |
1008	   255	|---|---|---|---|
1009	   256	| 1 | 2026-08-25 | update | Authored by owner decision as the check the lead-pm role runs on the lead-po role's output — the maker/checker split's named process. First process to carry `asks` and `ask-cap`. Criteria sets per artifact type (brief, product decision record, acceptance scenarios, backlog order) are a filed gap: until each exists, `criteria_path` names the nearest approved fitness set or the framing alone. |
1010	   257	| 1 | 2026-08-25 | review | Screened against the process-definition chain: findings — an uncovered finding could never clear the screen; the `review` type lacked per-finding criterion, quote, and decidability; two prompts wrote to undeclared channels; `artifact_type` loaded and unread; one route-decision branch dead; status values and the gap's home undefined. |
1011	   258	| 2 | 2026-08-25 | update | Reworked: a `screen-review` type carries findings with criterion, quote, and decidability; route-screen gains a definition exit when every finding is uncovered; decide routes straight to record; the artifact leaves the decider's inputs; `artifact_type` dropped; the gap is filed as a review entry in the named definition's history and returned as `gap_entry`; status values declared as this process's pending the typedefs. |
1012	   259	| 2 | 2026-08-25 | review | Re-screened: findings — decide's prompt opened an undeclared artifact; a framing-trace failure had no criterion name and so was never repaired; record wrote a file outside its outputs; a vacuous all-uncovered branch on an empty list; ask without an initial. |
1013	   260	| 3 | 2026-08-25 | update | Repairs: the PM role decides from the review alone, wobbly findings quote the whole passage; `framing` is a named criterion the maker repairs; record returns the written definition's path; the definition exit guarded on a non-empty list; `ask` initial null; status vocabulary moved to Data prose. The v1 entry's "nearest approved fitness set or the framing alone" is superseded by Data's rule. |
1014	   261	| 3 | 2026-08-25 | review | Re-screened (round 3): clean — all six scenarios pass, six rules hold; both paths traced; stumbles polished in place (verdict precedence at the cap; the framing criterion named in the type). |
1015	   262	| 3 | 2026-08-26 | state | draft → approved by the owner. |

=================== basis/glossary.md
     1	---
     2	type: glossary
     3	id: glossary
     4	owner: product-authority

    11	
    12	# Glossary
    13	
    14	## How the list combines
    15	
    16	The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
    17	name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
    18	terms uses one of these when one fits.
    19	
    20	## Terms
    21	
    22	- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
    23	  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
    24	- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
    25	  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
    26	- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
    27	  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
    28	- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
    29	  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
    30	- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
    31	  enums, required sections.
    32	- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
    33	  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
    34	- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
    35	  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
    36	- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
    37	  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
    38	- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
    39	  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
    40	  into every rendering.
    41	- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
    42	  scoring an artifact type's quality.
    43	- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
    44	  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
    45	- **role** — a named capability contract and set of accountabilities,
    46	  assigned by process steps to whoever fills it; sequencing lives in
    47	  process definitions, not roles.
    48	- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
    49	  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
    50	  definition).
    51	- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
    52	  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
    53	- **owner** — the role that approves changes to a definition; named in
    54	  every definition's frontmatter.
    55	- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
    56	  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
    57	- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
    58	  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
    59	- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
    60	  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
    61	- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
    62	  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
    63	  archive.
    64	- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
    65	  context it loads into: working (every activity), architecture (the
    66	  designed system), or experience (the product's interactions).
    67	- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
    68	  artifact, never loaded into context.
    69	- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
    70	  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
    71	- **anchor** — the governed record a conversation attaches to: a session
    72	  record, a review record, or a work item; carries the conversation's
    73	  state across transcript boundaries.
    74	- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
    75	  (anchor: a review record and its outcomes), or work (anchor: a work
    76	  item).
    77	- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
    78	  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
    79	- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority decides
    80	  on presented material. Replaces "sitting".
    81	- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
    82	  presented and the outcomes applied; each decision traces in the
    83	  changed artifacts' Document History, never in a standing ledger.
    84	- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
    85	  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
    86	- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
    87	  failsafe exit fires.
    88	- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, keep,
    89	  retire, or terminal, with its target.
    90	- **authority-call** — a row marker on a migration-plan row awaiting a
    91	  decision from the authority; not an action — the row has no effect and
    92	  is out of scope for any run until ruled.
    93	- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
    94	  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
    95	- **close-out** — the mechanical execution of the migration plan's
    96	  pre-decided retire and terminal actions: snapshot, delete, archive
    97	  move, a loud post-check, and the branch promotion; no review loop.
    98	  All stages run consecutively at cut-over.
    99	- **snapshot tag** — the annotated git tag (`pre-migration`) on `main`'s
   100	  pre-execution commit, preserving the full corpus for terminal-recovery;
   101	  after close-out a terminal record exists only there.
   102	- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
   103	  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
   104	- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
   105	  running, held, done, cancelled.
   106	- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
   107	  anchor, by inactivity or by an ask; a held run is resumed or
   108	  cancelled, never dropped.
   109	- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
   110	  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
   111	- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
   112	  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).
   113	- **Bounded Context** — a deliberately drawn region of the product with
   114	  one internal language, one model, and one set of contracts to other
   115	  regions; drawn by design, never discovered after the fact (Evans,
   116	  *Domain-Driven Design*).
   117	- **shop** — the entity that builds, operates, and evolves part of the
   118	  product. Two types: the lead shop (the system-level coordinator; owns
   119	  product-level artifacts and no Bounded Context) and the BC-shop (owns
   120	  and produces exactly one Bounded Context). By the owner's decision a
   121	  BC-shop is a component team in the product literature's sense: it
   122	  receives bounded work for its context and does not own a feature end
   123	  to end; a request that crosses contexts is decomposed above it, in
   124	  the initiative, never by the shops between themselves.
   125	- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
   126	  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
   127	  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
   128	  same shape whoever performs it.
   129	- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
   130	  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
   131	  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
   132	  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
   133	  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
   134	- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
   135	  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
   136	  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
   137	  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
   138	  kernel, or separate ways.
   139	- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
   140	  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
   141	  wording.
   142	- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
   143	  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
   144	  internals.
   145	- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
   146	  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, the
   147	  outcome it serves, and the contract it entered through; the
   148	  exclusive decision of `lead-pm`; written as the first section of an
   149	  initiative and nowhere else.
   150	- **initiative** — the product-level problem artifact: one problem
   151	  worth solving, stated for the product, with its framing, one
   152	  measured outcome, an appetite and no-gos, the feasibility and
   153	  usability attachments, and the solutions architect's decomposition;
   154	  made by the PM role, screened by the cold reviewer, bet on by the
   155	  authority; features are made from it.
   156	- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario in a feature that
   157	  states, as a requirement, what counts as done for one behavior;
   158	  co-produced by the PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop;
   159	  assigned to that context by a `@bounded-context:<name>` tag the
   160	  solutions architect writes; held in that shop's scenario register.
   161	- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
   162	  acceptance scenarios tagged to it across all features, with their
   163	  hashes and states; read in full across every context when a claim
   164	  spans contexts.
   165	- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
   166	  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
   167	  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
   168	  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
   169	- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
   170	  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
   171	  domain the question falls in.
   172	- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
   173	  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
   174	  contract between contexts.
   175	- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
   176	  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
   177	  PO role.
   178	- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
   179	  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
   180	  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
   181	  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
   182	  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
   183	  together as the `assistant` guideline.
   184	- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
   185	  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
   186	  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
   187	  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
   188	  role's exclusive domain.
   189	- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
   190	  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
   191	- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
   192	  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
   193	  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
   194	- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
   195	  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
   196	  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
   197	  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
   198	- **feature** — a Gherkin Feature: one capability from the user's or
   199	  agent's point of view — a narrative saying who, what, and the outcome
   200	  — with the acceptance scenarios that state what counts as done for
   201	  it; product-level, belonging to its framing or initiative; its
   202	  scenarios may be owned by several Bounded Contexts. The PO role's
   203	  artifact. (The per-shop *brief* was retired 2026-08-28; the
   204	  `decision-brief` to the authority is unrelated.)
   205	- **check of record** — the check whose verdict the definitions rely
   206	  on for an artifact when the role that makes it also holds the
   207	  authority that approves it; for the initiative, the cold reviewer's
   208	  screen.
   209	- **bet** — the authority's decision to spend an initiative's appetite:
   210	  the go/no-go, taken in a review, moving it from `proposed` to
   211	  `planned`.
   212	- **product decision record** — the PO role's record of one
   213	  product-level decision — decision, alternatives, consequences,
   214	  decider and right, reversibility; ADR and MADR forms; checked as PO
   215	  output.
   216	- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
   217	  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
   218	  provenance through every translation and delegation.
   219
